raw_response:
I farm only 7.8 mu, so I cannot spread myself too thin. My way is still mostly what I learned from years in the field and from watching other people in the village. Wheat and maize are my steady crops, because even if prices are not great every year, they keep grain coming and the land is familiar. Cotton gives me some cash, but it also takes more watching and more picking, so I will not put too much land into it. This year I will keep about 5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 2.8 mu in cotton. I do not want to gamble with a big change. Fertilizer is expensive, and well water costs money too, so I will use enough to protect yield, but not chase the very highest output. For wheat I will do base fertilizer plus one topdress, and irrigate around the key stages. For maize, because the turnaround after wheat is tight, I will keep tillage simple and sow quickly after harvest. For cotton, I will manage it a bit more carefully on the smaller area, because if insects come and I do not act in time, the loss is real.

I also have family members working off-farm, so labor at home is not always enough. That means I will keep the field work simple where I can, and hire a little help only when the timing is tight, especially for cotton picking and for the wheat harvest period. I am not doing the “best possible” plan on paper. I am doing the plan I can afford and finish on time.
